correctness.rationale: For every \(0<\kappa\le4\) and positive rate and horizon, the failure product expands exactly into the strict quadratic \(\kappa(s-s_0)^2+C\), with \(xy=e^{-\lambda T}\) and feasible \(s\) spanning \([2\sqrt q,1+q]\). Strict convexity in the scalar \(s\), the root parametrization and exact endpoint inequalities prove the entire optimizer list and all boundaries; the finite checker is supplementary. At \(\kappa=4\), an interval of length \(\log2/\lambda\) guarantees success. The standard-library verifier passed 204786 assertions.

value.rationale: The exact four-regime and reentrant-equality classification answers a motivated timing question that generic monotonic or Jensen heuristics miss: for peak success exceeding 3/4, equal fire-return spacing is optimal only at intermediate horizons, with unequal preferred on both sides and an initial skip-one-opportunity phase. The threshold positions and all global allocations are closed-form, useful as benchmarks and counterexamples for fire-regime planning models; this is not a field prescription.
